ShortDescription.Value: Build one city together over a dedicated server. Roads, zoning, terrain, policies, progression and mod settings sync live; a small server program holds the shared city on your PC or on a Linux box.

Publish.LongDescription:
Build one city with friends. A small server program holds the shared city and passes round what everyone does; the game talks to it through this mod. Run the server from your own PC with one click, or put it on a Linux or Windows box and leave it running for your group.
**What syncs live** - Roads, buildings, zoning, bulldozing, terrain, districts and transit lines appear on everyone's screen as they are placed. You also see the other players' tool ghosts: the road they are dragging out, the building under their cursor, the area they are drawing. - Taxes, budgets, service fees, city policies and building options. - Progression: a development node one player buys is bought for everyone, and the host's XP and development points are shared, so milestones arrive together. - One treasury. The host's balance is the city's balance. - Where everyone is: a ring where each player is looking, a dot under their mouse, their name over it. - Other mods' settings: Traffic Tool Essentials junction settings, the Traffic mod's lane connections and priority signs, and Road Builder's custom roads.
Farms, forestry, mines and oil fields are the one thing not sent live yet; they arrive with the next save.
**How a session works** Main menu > **Multiplayer**. **Host game** starts the server window next to your game and joins it; friends join your address and port (27015 unless you change it, forwarded on your router). **Join game** connects to a friend or to a dedicated server. Joining from the menu downloads the shared city and loads it.
In a city, the round button at the top of the right-hand stack opens the panel: save to the server, fetch the newer city, see who is on. Anyone can save. The host also saves on its own every few minutes, and whoever joins later gets the latest save.
When the host connects and the server already holds a city, the game asks: load last save, or new world. New world opens the map list, mod maps included, and the city you start replaces the one on the server.
The simulation itself still runs on each PC, so citizens and traffic are not identical everywhere. Everything you build is.
**Dedicated server** This is a dedicated-server mod. The server is a separate program, not the game, so it runs on a box without Cities: Skylines II installed. The same program that Host game opens is on GitHub as a download for Linux and Windows, with an install script that sets it up as a service. All settings sit in one server.json file (name, password, owner key, mod check, welcome message) and the server picks up edits on its own. It can follow a public Paradox playset and tell anyone it turns away exactly which mods they are missing, and it checks GitHub for newer releases.
Server downloads, source code and issues: github.com/DillanStephenson/Cities-Skylines-2---multiplayer-DEDICATED-SERVER
**Mods** Any mod is fine as long as everyone runs the same playset. The server compares mod lists, ignoring version numbers, and tells a rejected player which playset to activate.
**Credits** Made by Dillan Stephenson. Testing: Mayor William. Thanks to the makers of Traffic Tool Essentials, Traffic and Road Builder, whose mods this one learned to carry along.
Early access: play with people you know, keep your own saves, and report problems on GitHub.
Publish.ChangeLog: 0.3.2: Saves to the server go through the game's own save queue. Saving outside it could collide with the game's autosave and throw a null reference in the serializer, which is what one player hit. 0.3.1: Forced group sync. Options > Multiplayer > "Sync everyone every (minutes)" on the host: every so many minutes everyone stops behind a Syncing world box, the host's city goes up to the server and the others load it. The in-game panel has "Sync everyone now" for the host as well. 0.3.0: Back to the replay method that never crashed: while another player's build lands, the selection tool is active for a moment and your own tool comes back right after (up to two seconds of waiting first, and every build queued meanwhile lands in the same go). The two newer methods from 0.2.7 to 0.2.9 are gone; they left ghosts on screen until the next click and are the prime suspects for the crashes. Source of truth: the host (else the longest-connected player) holds the true city. When your game cannot recreate three of the others' builds within two minutes it has drifted; it then asks the host for a fresh save and loads it on its own, and stops replaying until it has. 0.2.9: Power cables and other nets built by another player now join the network on your side even when the exact junction they snapped to is not there: the piece attaches to the node or edge under that point instead of ending loose (loose cable ends carried no power, which is why electricity could work on one PC and not the other). Remote builds land without pausing your tool system (which could take the game down): your tool's own preview is simply held back for the few frames a build takes. The toolbar still keeps its selection. 0.2.8: Road Builder's custom roads sync: every custom road a player has goes to the others when the session starts, when someone joins and when a new one is made, so roads built with them replay everywhere; a build that needs a road not yet arrived waits for it. "Reload when someone else saves" no longer reloads while you have built something in the last two minutes. The in-game panel opens again from the round button in the right-hand stack and closes on its own when you leave the city. 0.2.7: You now see what the others are placing before they place it: the road they drag out, the building under their cursor, the area they draw, as a ghost in their colour. Other players' builds no longer reset your toolbar when they land: your tool is paused for a few frames instead of being switched away. Progression syncs: development nodes one player buys are bought on every PC, and the host's XP and development points are shared like the money, so milestones fire for everyone. Fixes the shared treasury not actually being applied on the other PCs. 0.2.6: The Traffic mod's lane connections and priority signs now follow whoever changes them. Fixes other players' games crashing when someone places a farm, forestry, mining or oil area: those areas are no longer sent live and arrive with the next save instead. When the host connects and the server already holds a city, the game asks whether to load it or start a new world (map list opens, mod maps included). Fetching the server's city on purpose no longer re-uploads it as a new one. 0.2.5: Traffic Tool Essentials settings now follow the player who changes them (junction signals, phases, lane groups, lane directions, labels, sync groups, depot zones). New city button on the Join screen: the host starts a fresh city on any map and it replaces the one on the server. A player is told when their build could not be recreated on someone else's PC. Connections survive 30 s of silence; the server window no longer freezes when clicked; its console no longer logs every player-position update. 0.2.4: the mod's own Paradox entry no longer counts in mod-list checks (subscribers were seen as having an extra mod). Dedicated servers now read all settings from server.json and reload it live. 0.2.3: first published build. Server window, shared city, live build sync (roads, buildings, zoning, terrain, transit lines), city settings and building options sync, shared treasury, player markers on the map, anyone can save, menu screens, in-game panel, playset-aware mod check, server update check.
